_comment: 2026 Senate cycle configuration for the control simulation. Every seat on the 2026 ballot is simulated: the 33 Class II seats plus the Ohio and Florida specials (35 races). dem_safe_seats / rep_safe_seats are therefore the holdovers only: Democrats (with the two independents who caucus with them) hold 47 seats of which 13 are up, so dem_safe = 34; Republicans hold 53 of which 22 are up, so rep_safe = 31. dem_majority_threshold is 51 because the sitting VP (R) breaks 50-50 ties. Fundamentals: each race carries the state's Dem-minus-Rep presidential margin in 2024 and 2020; the fundamentals prior blends them (pres_weight_recent on 2024), adds the national swing, and is blended into the polling margin with weight blend_k/(blend_k+num_polls), so a race with no polls runs on the prior alone and the prior fades as polls accumulate. A null dem_candidate / rep_candidate means the nominee was not settled when this was written: the Wikipedia scraper then tracks that party's most-polled candidate and the export uses the resolved name. held_by is the party defending the seat (used for safe-seat arithmetic and the predictions board). wikipedia overrides the default article title (Ohio and Florida are special elections). Nominees were confirmed 2026-11-02 against the full 2026 slate (general-election polling tables, Kalshi tickers, and a hand check).

forecast._comment: calibration_bias_weight scales the historically-fitted poll bias (~-2.5) before it is applied: 0 = ignore it (fundamentals already capture the red-state lean), 1 = apply in full, 0.5 = split the difference. Kept at 0.5 to avoid double-counting the same Dem-overstatement that the fundamentals blend also corrects.
forecast._tail_comment: Student-t degrees of freedom for polling error (variance-matched to the calibrated sigmas; null = Gaussian). Backtest on the 98 calibration races: t(5) Brier 0.0591 / log-loss 0.1905 vs Gaussian 0.0602 / 0.1952 — fat tails score better on both, and t(5) is the standard middle in the literature. Recomputed monthly in forecast_calibration.json under tail_comparison.

national_environment._comment: The midterm climate, applied as a uniform swing on top of each state's presidential lean (so the fundamentals prior reflects today, not 2024). Expected national Dem-minus-Rep margin = generic_weight*generic_ballot + approval_weight*(approval-implied margin for the out-party); the swing is that minus the 2024 House baseline. president_party is the in-party that pays the midterm penalty. approval_to_margin_coef converts the president's net approval to their party's national margin. senate_responsiveness scales how much of the national swing reaches Senate races. It only moves the fundamentals prior — polled races already price the climate in, so this mainly lifts thinly-polled seats.

Open seat (Daines not running). Three-way race: Alme (R), Bodnar (independent) and Bankhead (D). The polling tables show Alme 38-47 vs Bankhead 10-25, i.e. Bodnar holds the anti-Alme vote, so like Nebraska the independent occupies the Dem column and the model tracks Alme vs Bodnar. A Bodnar win is counted as a Dem seat for control, which overstates certainty about whom he would caucus with.

Osborn is an independent with no Democratic nominee of note; he occupies the Dem column so the race has a two-way margin. A win is counted as a Dem seat for control, which overstates certainty about whom he would caucus with.
